why: codex refuses to start outside a git repository unless --skip-git-repo-check is passed, and 'ask' is the default autonomy — without this flag the common case fails before producing a single event. Confirmed against the real binary

the flag is DELIBERATELY ABSENT once writes are possible. Codex wants a repo so its edits stay recoverable, and that concern is real here. Passing it unconditionally — which this core did until it was checked — silently removed the only safety net between a write-capable bot and an unrecoverable folder
the top of the ladder, reached only after the user typed a confirmation
order is load-bearing: the subcommand and its thread id come before flags, and the prompt is positional and last. '-m' and '-C' are the short forms codex accepts

MCP config paths are NOT forwarded to codex. Servers are registered out of band with `codex mcp`, once per host, so an implementation that helpfully passes them per run invents a flag codex does not have
an unrecognised trust level falls to the most restrictive sandbox. It must never be read as more trust than was granted
